title: PAN vs. VAT in Nepal: Understanding the Differences (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Understand the legal differences between PAN and VAT in Nepal. Discover mandatory registration thresholds, filing deadlines, and penalty rules.
h1: PAN vs. VAT in Nepal: Understanding the Difference
directAnswer: The fundamental difference between PAN and VAT in Nepal is that a Permanent Account Number (PAN) is a mandatory nine-digit identification number issued by the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) for tracking all taxable transactions and income tax, while Value Added Tax (VAT) is a specific indirect consumption tax (13%) levied on value addition for businesses meeting statutory turnover thresholds (NPR 20 Lakhs for services, NPR 50 Lakhs for goods).
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.h2: PAN vs. VAT: Core Conceptual & Legal Distinctions
sections.contentHtml:
A frequent point of confusion among new entrepreneurs in Lalitpur and Kathmandu is treating PAN and VAT as mutually exclusive options. In reality, **PAN (Permanent Account Number)** is the mandatory unique tax identification issued by the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) to every registered taxpayer. **VAT (Value Added Tax)** is a consumption tax administered under the VAT Act 2052 that attaches to your existing PAN certificate once specific statutory thresholds or business activities are triggered.

AttributeIncome Tax PAN (General PAN)VAT Registration (13% VAT)
Legal RequirementMandatory for every business & entityMandatory upon hitting turnover limits or specified sectors
Tax Rate ChargedZero indirect tax charged on sales13% statutory tax added to customer invoices

Filing FrequencyQuarterly advance tax & annual returnMonthly Form 13 return due before 25th

sections.h2: Statutory Turnover Thresholds & Mandatory VAT Sectors
sections.contentHtml:
Under the latest Inland Revenue Department directives, businesses must register under VAT when either of the following conditions is satisfied:

  • Turnover Thresholds (Trailing 12 Months): Commercial goods transactions exceeding NPR 50 Lakhs, or professional/consultancy services exceeding NPR 20 Lakhs, or mixed goods and service operations exceeding NPR 20 Lakhs.
  • Mandatory Sector Inclusions (Regardless of Turnover): Hardware suppliers, sanitary goods, educational and health consultancy desks, liquor and beverage stores, brick manufacturers, transport vehicle operations, software development agencies, and entities dealing in specified commercial corridors.
  • Government & Institutional Procurement: Participating in public tenders or billing government agencies, UN bodies, or licensed corporate entities generally mandates full 13% VAT registration.

Once enrolled in VAT, the business enters a strict monthly reporting regime. By the 25th day of every Nepali month, the enterprise must upload Form 13 sales and purchase registers to the IRD portal. Even during months with zero commercial revenue, filing a **Nil Return** is mandatory. Missing the 25th deadline incurs automatic compounding fines under Section 19 of the VAT Act 2052.

faqs.question: Can a business voluntarily register for VAT before reaching turnover thresholds?
faqs.answer: Yes. Voluntary VAT registration is common for B2B enterprises that sell to VAT-registered corporate clients who require formal tax invoices to claim input credits.

faqs.question: What happens if our turnover exceeds the threshold but we do not register for VAT?
faqs.answer: The IRD will conduct a retrospective tax assessment, demand 13% VAT on all past sales out of your pocket, and impose fines of up to 100% plus statutory late-fee interest.
